groups.sentence: Course rules and AI policies are provisional and may change during the term.
Guidance is a living document that will be updated and will evolve as AI technology and practice change.
Community members may submit feedback, suggestions and comments on the policy.
Policies and guidance are reviewed on a stated periodic schedule, usually at least annually, by a named body.
AI policies are still under development, and further guidance or policy documents are forthcoming.
AI tools, practices and citation norms are changing quickly, so rules cannot cover everything.
The university reviews and updates its AI policy and guidance regularly, such as annually.
Policy documents list their review dates, version history or update status.
Instructors revisit and update their course AI policy and syllabus language each term as AI changes.
The university collects community feedback and uses it to improve its policies and resources.
Administrators set up committees, working groups or ongoing discussions to keep addressing AI issues.
Designated bodies recommend revisions or updates to the policy.
Policy changes are documented, archived and communicated to the campus.
Instructors communicate any changes to the course AI policy to students in writing.
Students and community members stay informed of policy updates and keep consulting current policies.
Everyone in teaching, learning and research adapts to the growing field of AI.
